title: Modi Lands in Slovakia. No Indian Prime Minister Has Set Foot There Since 1993.
excerpt: Bilateral trade has doubled to €1.6 billion in three years. The first-ever visit comes as the India-EU Free Trade Agreement opens new doors for Slovak and Indian businesses alike.
body:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi arrived in Slovakia on Sunday for a state visit that no Indian leader has made in over three decades. It is the first time a sitting Indian Prime Minister has visited the Central European nation since it gained independence from Czechoslovakia in 1993.

Modi is in Bratislava at the invitation of Slovak Prime Minister Robert Fico. The two leaders are expected to hold delegation-level talks covering trade, investment, automobile manufacturing and railway infrastructure. Modi will also meet Slovak President Peter Pellegrini, who welcomed the visit on X, calling it "historic" and saying it would "open new opportunities for Slovakia-India cooperation."

## A Trade Relationship That Has Quietly Doubled

The headline numbers are striking. India-Slovakia bilateral trade has jumped from €800 million to €1.6 billion between 2023 and 2025 — one of the sharpest accelerations India has seen with any European partner in recent years. Slovak Ambassador to India Robert Maxian described the recently concluded India-EU Free Trade Agreement as the "mother of deals," telling NDTV he expects it to double trade figures further and significantly boost two-way investment.

Five major Slovak business groups have visited India in the last three years to expand commercial ties. During the visit, Modi is expected to meet CEOs of several major Slovak companies that have already invested in India.

India's Ambassador to Slovakia, Apoorva Srivastava, described the visit as significant for more than diplomacy. "This trip will not only strengthen our political relations, but also economic security and people-to-people contacts," she told IANS. She also pointed out that Slovakia launched its own Indo-Pacific strategy in December 2025, giving "a lot of importance to the Indo-Pacific region, not only trade and technology, but also to increasing the political relationship."

## A Relationship Built on Quiet Goodwill

The two countries share a history that predates Slovak independence. India recognised Slovakia immediately after its formation in 1993 and has maintained steady, if modest, diplomatic ties since.

One moment stands out. During Russia's invasion of Ukraine in 2022, Slovakia played a critical role in evacuating Indian nationals. A total of 1,113 Indian students and two foreign nationals were evacuated through Slovak territory during Operation Ganga — a fact that New Delhi has not forgotten.

The visit also follows recent high-level exchanges. Slovak President Pellegrini visited India for the AI Impact Summit in New Delhi in February 2026, where he and Modi reviewed bilateral ties and discussed cooperation in startups, IT, renewable energy, manufacturing, defence, space and education. Before that, India's President Droupadi Murmu undertook a state visit to Slovakia in April 2025.

## What Comes Next: The G7 and VivaTech

After Slovakia, Modi returns to France for the second leg of his European tour. He will participate in the G7 Summit in Evian on June 16-17, where he is expected to push Global South priorities and hold a bilateral meeting with US President Donald Trump — their first face-to-face since the diplomatic tensions sparked by the killing of Indian sailors in the Strait of Hormuz.

Modi will then travel to Paris for the VivaTech Summit, Europe's largest technology and startup event, and is expected to address members of the Indian diaspora community during his Paris stop.

For NRIs in Europe, the visit signals a deepening of India's economic footprint in Central and Eastern Europe. The India-EU FTA is expected to lower trade barriers across the bloc, and Slovakia — with its strong automotive and manufacturing base — could emerge as a gateway for Indian companies looking to set up or expand operations on the continent.

The visit is short, but the groundwork is three decades overdue.
